summary: In 2017 attackers took personal data on about 145 million people from Equifax over 76 days. The US GAO found weaknesses in Equifax's patching, detection and network design. This file uses a trade-press summary of the GAO report because the GAO page itself could not be read.

overview.background: Equifax is a credit reporting company. The attack began with a flaw in the Apache Struts web framework in a web application.
systems: An internet-facing web application using Apache Struts
A dispute-resolution server with an outdated certificate
overview.impact: Personal information of about 145 million people in the US, Canada and the UK was taken, according to the summary.
overview.severity: A major breach. The summary reports at least 9,000 queries to 51 databases over 76 days.
overview.gaps: The summary does not say whether Equifax had patched the flaw, and gives no dates. This file does not add any.

archNote: Components and relationships come from the cited source where it describes them. Layout and labels are ours.

diagrams.title: A weak first system and a long, quiet intrusion
diagrams.caption: Per the summary: attackers began scanning for the flaw within two days of public disclosure, queried 51 databases at least 9,000 times over 76 days, and encrypted traffic with an outdated certificate to avoid inspection.

nodes.label: Web application with the Struts flaw
Traffic hidden by an outdated certificate

diagrams.title: Segmentation, query limits and certificate hygiene (conceptual)
diagrams.caption: General guards linked to the GAO's findings: network architecture, query limits and inspection.

afterChanges: A first foothold cannot reach every database.
afterNote: The after picture shows the corrective ideas in the source and general good practice. It is conceptual unless the source says otherwise.
timelineNote: Times are as published by the source. Entries without a clock time are given in order only.

timeline.e: A flaw in Apache Struts is publicly disclosed.
Attackers begin scanning for the flaw, per the summary.
Attackers get in and run queries against many databases.
They make at least 9,000 queries to 51 databases and remove data in small pieces.
Equifax detects the intrusion after a delay, per the summary.
Equifax says it has fixed the issues; the GAO has not independently verified the fixes.

rootCause.trigger: An attacker exploited a known web framework flaw.
rootCause.underlying: Equifax did not find the flaw or the intrusion quickly, per the summary.
contributing: No limit on queries from a single address
An outdated certificate hid traffic from inspection

evidence.label: Query limits
evidence.body: a failure to establish limits on the number of database queries possible from a single address
evidence.note: As quoted in the Dark Reading summary of the GAO report.

evidence.label: Remediation status
evidence.body: Equifax states it has fixed the issues; the GAO has not verified them.
evidence.note: A restatement of the summary; not a quotation.

diagnose.step: Check certificate expiry on inspection points.

fix.safety: Do not run scanning against systems you do not own.

troubleshoot.scenario: A framework you use has a critical flaw announced today. You do not know every application that uses it.
troubleshoot.question: What is your first day plan?
hints: How do you check for abuse?
troubleshoot.answer: Inventory, patch internet-facing apps first, look for exploitation, segment and review databases for unusual queries.

rootcause.q: How many databases did attackers query?

remediation.answer: Per source rate limits for bulk access.
Separate web tier from data stores.

design.prompt: Design detection for slow data theft.
design.answer: Per-source query baselines, egress monitoring, working inspection and tested alerts.

checks.q: How long did the intrusion last, per the summary?
About how many people were affected?
Does this file say whether Equifax had patched?
options: No, the summary does not say

verification: Facts come from Dark Reading's summary of the GAO report (read 29 October 2026). The GAO page (the card source) was not read, so details beyond the summary are not claimed. The second evidence item is a restatement and is labelled Simulated.
